blind_target.title: Association of e-cigarette vaping and progression to heavier patterns of cigarette smoking
blind_target.evidence_quote: In this paper, we present a replication study with new data using the same protocol as the cornerstone study by Leventhal et al.21 22
blind_target.outcome_quote: For this study, we replicated an American cornerstone study21 22 on the association between e-cigarette use and tobacco smoking in the Netherlands and Flanders and found similar results.

shipped_originals.title_o: Sex Differences: A Study of the Eye of the Beholder

blind_target.evidence_quote: This was tested using a conceptual replication of an influential gender label study by Condry and Condry in which participants viewed a video of a baby crying in response to a startling event.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Contrary to the Condry findings, this study found that participant perception of why a baby was crying was not consistent with the gender label given (consistent, being angry for the boy label and fearful for the girl label). Participant ratings did not vary significantly based on the gender label.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract directly contrasts the tested gender-label finding with the original; reference details are absent.

shipped_originals.title_o: The activation of word class information during speech production.

blind_target.authors: Pechmann, T.; Garrett, M. F.; Zerbst, D.
blind_target.title: The time course of recovery for grammatical class information during lexical processing for syntactic construction
blind_target.evidence_quote: If the word class effect observed here and by Pechmann and colleagues (2004 ; Pechmann & Zerbst, 2002 ) does not reflect a lexical effect, it would remove such evidence as support for models that assume word class constraints on lexical selection (e.g., Dell et al., 2008 ). In Experiment 2, we tried to establish whether a word class effect could be obtained when the variable imageability was controlled.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Experiment 2 revealed that the word class effect could not be separated from the imageability effect: Naming latencies were sensitive to distractor imageability (see Lupker, 1979 ), but were not sensitive to distractor word class when imageability was controlled. These results conflict with the results of Pechmann and colleagues (2004 ; Pechmann & Zerbst, 2002 ).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly compare the tested word class effects to this original; outcome follows the reported agreement and disagreement.

blind_target.evidence_quote: Jones and Westoff (1979) reported a study of fertility trends among white women in intact first marriages.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We found that the fertility of the two religious groups was indeed converging, but the Catholic-non-Catholic differential was larger than that found by Jones and Westoff --how much larger depends on what measure is used. Moreover, we found that the differential by frequency of communion among Catholic wives was not converging.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract reports agreement on fertility convergence between religious groups but disagreement on convergence by communion frequency.

shipped_originals.title_o: Attention control, memory updating, and emotion regulation temporarily reduce the capacity for executive control.

blind_target.authors: Healey MK, Hasher L, Danilova E
blind_target.title: The stability of working memory: Do previous tasks influence complex span?
blind_target.evidence_quote:
In this study, for the depletion task, we used the actual video material and verbatim instructions from the popular video-viewing attention control task employed by prior researchers. For the outcome task, we used a complex working memory span task known as the operation span task (OSPAN; [
36
]). We selected these particular tasks because they maximize the chances of demonstrating the ego-depletion effect for the following reasons: a) the video-viewing attention control task is one of the most widely used tasks and has consistently been shown to induce ego-depletion in prior research (e.g., [
5
,
31
–
33
]); b) the OSPAN task places heavy demand on executive attention and hence should tax self-control resources (e.g., [
37
]); c) this particular combination of tasks has produced medium to large effect sizes in prior studies [
5
,
38
]; d) these tasks are matched in terms of stimulus modality (i.e., both tasks utilize words), which has been shown to amplify the ego-depletion effect [
38
].
blind_target.outcome_quote: Contrary to the ego-depletion hypothesis, participants in the depletion condition did not perform worse than control participants on the subsequent self-control task, even after considering moderator variables.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The task combination is explicitly linked to these two prior effect demonstrations; the present attempt finds no depletion effect.
